clue.text: Actor's firm substitute for given name of drug

indicators.note: the actor's first name is swapped out and the firm's short form put in its place

parts.note: Michael Caine is the veteran British film actor
CO is the usual abbreviation for company, a firm

explanation.surface: A stand-in for some actor's company, named in the credits, is mixed up with drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: Drop MICHAEL from MICHAEL CAINE and put CO in its place.
explanation.definitionFit: Cocaine is a stimulant narcotic, a classic example of an illegal drug.

clue.text: I'm a cheque that bounced, producing folds

indicators.note: a bounced cheque comes back, so the phrase before it is read backwards

parts.note: taken as written, the apostrophe dropped
a giro is a British state benefit cheque

explanation.surface: Someone confesses to being a bad cheque, and the business folds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that bounced' turns IMAGIRO round. A GIRO is a British benefit payment cheque.
explanation.definitionFit: Origami is the Japanese craft of paper folding, so the art is defined by its folds.

clue.text: On a diet, perhaps including those in charge above

indicators.note: the jumbled phrase wraps round the people in charge
perhaps hints that the letters of the dieting phrase may be arranged differently

parts.note: foremen are the supervisors in charge of workers

explanation.surface: Bosses watching their weight are mentioned as being on a diet.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as A FOR E MENTIONED, the answer states the theme: every clue that cites '3' wants a word with an A put where its E was.
explanation.definitionFit: Something described above in a text has been referred to earlier, the meaning of this formal word.

clue.text: Treatment for refusal to play guitar?

parts.note: no is a refusal
to strum is to play a guitar by brushing the strings

explanation.surface: A musician who won't pick up the guitar needs some kind of therapy.
explanation.definitionFit: A nostrum is a quack remedy, a supposed cure or treatment of doubtful worth.

clue.text: Wrap-up warm 3

indicators.note: the reference to 3 down, read as a phrase, says to put the first vowel in place of the second

parts.note: summery weather is warm

explanation.surface: Wrap up warm, the clue seems to advise.
explanation.walkthrough: Change the E of SUMMERY to A.
explanation.definitionFit: A wrap-up is a closing recap of the main points, which is what a précis gives.

clue.text: Unattached, I am promoted as one

indicators.note: in a down answer promotion moves a letter higher up the word

parts.note: untied means not fastened or unattached
taken as written

explanation.surface: A single person announces a promotion and a new partnership.
explanation.walkthrough: 'am promoted' lifts the I of UNTIED two places up the column.
explanation.definitionFit: United means joined together, acting together as a single body.

clue.text: See 3
Find a new way out in note after note

indicators.note: the first musical piece follows the second note, so the second note goes in front

parts.note: re again, the sol-fa note

indicators.note: the word for away is placed inside the first note

parts.note: re is the second note of the sol-fa scale
taken as written

explanation.surface: A musician seeks a way out of the score, one note after another.
explanation.definitionFit: To reroute is to send along a different path, finding another course.

clue.text: One rings to complain as Guardian leader is incorrectly spelt

indicators.note: a word spelt wrongly has its letters out of order, so these letters are rearranged
the leader of a word is its opening letter

explanation.surface: A reader phones in to grumble that the newspaper's editorial contains a spelling mistake.
explanation.walkthrough: The Guardian is famous for typos; 'is' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A campanologist is a bell-ringer, someone who rings church bells.

clue.text: Sounds like food: hello and goodbye!

indicators.note: the clue says the word for food is said aloud

parts.note: chow is slang for food

explanation.surface: Someone notes that a greeting rhymes with grub.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian greeting is used both on meeting and on parting.

clue.text: 3 needed to write still

indicators.note: the reference to 3 down, read as a phrase, says to put the first vowel in place of the second

parts.note: stationery is paper, pens and other writing materials

explanation.surface: Some writing materials are all one needs to write a novel at a standstill.
explanation.walkthrough: STATIONERY with A for its E gives the adjective, a famously confused pair.
explanation.definitionFit: Stationary means not moving, the same sense as still.

clue.text: Nurse accepts the end of the profession

indicators.note: the nurse takes in another letter, so it goes inside

parts.note: a carer nurses or looks after someone

indicators.note: the end of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: A nurse accepts that her working life is coming to an end.
explanation.definitionFit: A career is one's lifelong line of work, as is a profession.

clue.text: Former minister trapped by how he should be

indicators.note: the minister is held inside the word that follows

parts.note: a minister ought to be devout, pious
Rev is short for Reverend, a minister's title

explanation.surface: An ex-clergyman is caught out by the standard of behaviour expected of him.
explanation.definitionFit: Previous means earlier or prior, as does former.

clue.text: Weapon provided backing for a vault

indicators.note: one piece stands in place of a letter, so it is substituted

parts.note: an armament is a weapon
taken as written

indicators.note: backing means reversed, read from the end

parts.note: if means provided, on condition that

explanation.surface: A weapon's support is given for a pole-vaulter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' turns IF into FI, which replaces the first A of ARMAMENT.
explanation.definitionFit: The firmament is the vault of heaven, the arched sky.

clue.text: Sad musical with less entourage

indicators.note: the outer letters, the surroundings of the title, are removed

parts.note: Les Misérables is the long-running stage musical

explanation.surface: A gloomy show that is staged without its supporting cast.
explanation.walkthrough: Strip LES from the front and S from the back of the show's title.
explanation.definitionFit: Miserable means unhappy, the same state as sad.

clue.text: It points to home of French kiss

parts.note: to be in is to be at home
de is French for of
X is the kiss written at the end of a letter

explanation.surface: Someone's finger points to the source of the French kiss.
explanation.definitionFit: An index finger is the pointer, and a book's index points to pages.

clue.text: Expose oneself to meat if 3

indicators.note: the reference to 3 down, read as a phrase, says to put the first vowel in place of the second

parts.note: flesh is meat

explanation.surface: A flasher bares his body to whoever is mentioned.
explanation.walkthrough: Change the E of FLESH to A.
explanation.definitionFit: To flash is slang for exposing oneself indecently in public.

clue.text: Draw sleek creature in lovely shell

indicators.note: the animal goes inside the edges of the next word
a shell is the outside, so the first and last letters

parts.note: the otter is a sleek-furred water mammal

explanation.surface: Someone draws an otter inside a pretty seashell.
explanation.definitionFit: A lottery is a draw for prizes, decided by chance.

clue.text: Poor clue compiler had troubled to explain

indicators.note: a poor clue is badly made, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: the setter refers to themselves as I, so 'compiler had' is I'd
ate means troubled, as in what's eating you

explanation.surface: A setter regrets a bad clue and must make it clear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poor' makes ELUC from CLUE; 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To elucidate is to make clear, to explain.

clue.text: Feeling mortified? What you need is tea and a smile

parts.note: cha (or char) is British slang for tea
a grin is a smile

explanation.surface: Advice that a cup of tea and a smile will cheer up the embarrassed.
explanation.definitionFit: Chagrin is the vexed embarrassment of having been humiliated.

clue.text: Beat man to the touchline

parts.note: to tan someone's hide is to beat them
gent is short for gentleman, a man

explanation.surface: A winger beats his man and races to the touchline.
explanation.definitionFit: A tangent is a line that touches a curve at one point.

clue.text: Fix the Guardian's severity

parts.note: to rig is to fix dishonestly
the newspaper speaking of itself says our

explanation.surface: The paper's rigged strictness is exposed.
explanation.definitionFit: Rigour means strictness or harshness, synonymous with severity.

clue.text: 3 money for bird

indicators.note: the reference to 3 down, read as a phrase, says to put the first vowel in place of the second

parts.note: sterling is British money

explanation.surface: The cash for a bird is mentioned.
explanation.walkthrough: Change the first E of STERLING to A.
explanation.definitionFit: The starling is a common speckled songbird.

clue.text: 3 motor is a pain

indicators.note: the reference to 3 down, read as a phrase, says to put the first vowel in place of the second

parts.note: an engine is a motor

explanation.surface: The car's engine is giving trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: The instruction applies to every E, so both Es of ENGINE become As at once; 'is' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Angina is chest pain caused by poor blood flow to the heart.

clue.text: Hang on, Eritrea is not entirely a lost cause

indicators.note: only part of the phrase is used, the answer sitting within its words

explanation.surface: An appeal to wait: the African country's position is not quite hopeless.
explanation.definitionFit: A goner is someone or something beyond saving, a lost cause.

clue.text: Arachne's home worse off after burglar emptied software

indicators.note: the jumbled word follows the emptied burglar

parts.note: Arachne was turned into a spider in Greek myth, so her home is a web

indicators.note: emptying a word leaves only its outer letters
something off has gone wrong, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A spider's lair is in a worse state after a burglar cleaned it out.
explanation.definitionFit: A web browser is the software program used to view internet pages.

clue.text: Born and died in poverty

parts.note: née, French for born, introduces a maiden name

explanation.surface: Someone was born and died poor.
explanation.definitionFit: Need is want or lack of means, which is poverty.

clue.text: Spooner's greeting to Simpson with total recall

indicators.note: Dr Spooner swapped the opening sounds of words

parts.note: hi is a greeting
Bart Simpson of the cartoon family

explanation.surface: Someone recalls perfectly the greeting to a cartoon character.
explanation.walkthrough: Swap the opening sounds of HI BART to say BY HEART.
explanation.definitionFit: Knowing something by heart means memorised completely, perfect recall.

clue.text: One does not appreciate where coal may be found

definitions.meaning: an ungrateful person who shows no thanks
coal burns in a grate, so it is found within one

explanation.definitionFit: An ingrate is an ungrateful person, one who doesn't appreciate kindness.
